sources.title: Rust 1.97.0 release notes and Edition 2024/Cargo resolver 3 documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: Published by the Rust Project on doc.rust-lang.org; release notes and Edition Guide are primary toolchain sources.
sources.freshness_signals: Rust 1.97.0 is dated 2026-07-09; stable documentation accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Confirms the exact compiler baseline, Edition 2024 stabilization, resolver 3 behavior, and the requirement to set resolver=3 explicitly in a virtual workspace.
sources.notes: Related official page: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/edition-guide/rust-2024/cargo-resolver.html . Resolver 3's Rust-version fallback is not a substitute for a locked all-feature build on Rust 1.97; preserve Cargo.lock and verify every package MSRV. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Tokio runtime, bounded mpsc, cancellation, and graceful-shutdown documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: Tokio project-owned tutorial and generated API documentation linked to maintained source.
sources.freshness_signals: Current Rustdoc showed Tokio 1.52.3; pages accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines supervision, CancellationToken, TaskTracker, bounded queue backpressure, clean shutdown, and the failure boundaries needed for bounded local services.
sources.notes: Related API page: https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/mpsc/ . The docs distinguish bounded channels from infinite-capacity unbounded channels. Overflow quarantine/resynchronization is an application policy, and unbounded queues must not carry execution-critical events. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Serde, Reqwest, and Tokio-Tungstenite transport boundary documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: Crate Rustdoc links to the canonical source repositories; Serde also has a project-owned documentation site.
sources.freshness_signals: Reqwest 0.13.4 and Tokio-Tungstenite 0.30.0 were current; the latter is dated 2026-07-11.
sources.selection_rationale: Covers typed serialization, reusable asynchronous HTTP, TLS and redirect policy, streamed bodies, and Tokio-integrated WebSocket Stream/Sink APIs.
sources.notes: Related pages: https://serde.rs/ and https://docs.rs/tokio-tungstenite/latest/tokio_tungstenite/ . Reqwest documents system proxies enabled by default, so production configuration must explicitly decide proxy behavior, endpoint allowlists, TLS backend, redirects, and timeouts. These libraries do not provide venue sequence/checksum validation. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Apache Arrow Rust, native Parquet, CSV, and JSON ingestion documentation family
sources.source_type: official Apache Software Foundation project documentation
sources.credibility_signals: Apache Arrow-owned API documentation; Parquet page identifies itself as the official native Rust implementation.
sources.freshness_signals: Current Arrow family documentation and Parquet 59.1.0 accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Directly documents RecordBatch, explicit schemas, CSV/JSON/IPC readers and writers, Serde conversion, and Arrow-to-Parquet persistence APIs.
sources.notes: Related official page: https://arrow.apache.org/rust/parquet/index.html . Parquet partitioning, compaction, manifests, deduplication, and point-in-time semantics are application responsibilities. Bound schema inference and treat experimental content-defined chunking as non-baseline. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Apache DataFusion embedded analytical query engine documentation
sources.source_type: official Apache Software Foundation project documentation
sources.credibility_signals: Apache DataFusion primary documentation under ASF governance, with API docs, architecture, configuration, and examples.
sources.selection_rationale: Establishes the embeddable Rust SQL/DataFrame engine over Arrow with native CSV, JSON, and Parquet sources.
sources.notes: Production integration must configure memory/runtime limits, cancellation, and controlled local table providers; unrestricted SQL, arbitrary URLs, and broad extension loading must not be exposed via MCP. DataFusion remains outside the live path and its fast release cadence requires a locked tested version. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: SQLite control-plane database documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: Primary SQLite project documentation for SQL, C API, WAL, isolation, threading, integrity, and file format.
sources.freshness_signals: Current pages include 2025-2026 updates and were accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Supports local transactional configuration, cursors, manifests, registries, and run state while documenting concurrency and integrity constraints.
sources.notes: Related pages: https://www.sqlite.org/foreignkeys.html and https://www.sqlite.org/stricttables.html . Foreign-key enforcement is off by default per connection; STRICT needs SQLite 3.37+. WAL improves concurrency but SQLite still has a single-writer model and must not be queried per live event. Configure busy handling, migrations, backups, and integrity checks explicitly. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-11-25 stdio, tools, schema, progress, and cancellation specification family
sources.credibility_signals: Authoritative Model Context Protocol specification on the protocol's official domain.
sources.freshness_signals: The site marked protocol version 2025-11-25 as latest on 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines local subprocess stdio framing, protocol-clean stdout, JSON-RPC lifecycle/version negotiation, typed tool schemas and structured results, progress, and cancellation.
sources.notes: Related pages: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools and https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/utilities/cancellation . Ordinary cancellation is advisory and race-prone; task-augmented requests use tasks/cancel. Schemas do not replace authorization, bounded results, audit, or risk enforcement. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Coinbase Exchange WebSocket channels and book/trade integrity documentation
sources.credibility_signals: Coinbase Developer Platform documentation for the Exchange API and live channel schemas.
sources.freshness_signals: Active Exchange changelog and current docs accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Documents heartbeats and sequence/trade identifiers, status and precision, full order events, REST snapshot plus queued update replay, level2 snapshots and absolute-size updates, and trades.
sources.notes: Related best-practices page: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/websocket-feed/best-practices . Matches-only messages can be dropped and recovered via heartbeat/trade IDs; zero level2 size deletes a level. Channel authentication and integrity fields vary, and no level2 checksum is documented. Keep Coinbase DirectUnverified until the exact selected channel proves sequence, freshness, status, precision, and resync requirements end to end. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Kraken WebSocket v2 order-book checksum and maintenance guide
sources.credibility_signals: Canonical Kraken Developers guide with an exact algorithm and deterministic fixture.
sources.freshness_signals: Current canonical v2 URL reached from Kraken's redirect and accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Specifies CRC32 over the top ten levels, decimal-preserving parsing, update ordering, delete-on-zero, depth truncation, normalization, and an expected checksum fixture.
sources.notes: Checksum verification is optional upstream but should be mandatory for executable qualification. It covers only the top ten levels; deeper-book correctness and reconnect/status/timestamp semantics need companion reference review and tests. Quarantine and resubscribe on any mismatch. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: SEC EDGAR submissions, company facts, XBRL frames, and bulk archives documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: SEC .gov primary documentation for data.sec.gov and EDGAR public data.
sources.freshness_signals: Last reviewed 2025-04-08; current update schedules and endpoints accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Covers unauthenticated submissions and XBRL JSON APIs, freshness, nightly bulk files, CORS limitations, and the scope limitations of standardized company facts.
sources.notes: Related policy page: https://www.sec.gov/about/webmaster-frequently-asked-questions . SEC requires a declared User-Agent and documents a 10 requests/second maximum for equitable access. Prefer nightly bulk ZIPs for large backfills, cache locally, preserve filing/accession evidence, and do not treat frames' calendar alignment as issuer fiscal-period truth. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: FRED and ALFRED REST API, real-time periods, and vintage dates documentation family
sources.source_type: official Federal Reserve Bank API documentation
sources.credibility_signals: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis primary API documentation for FRED and ALFRED.
sources.freshness_signals: Current endpoint and real-time-period pages accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Documents JSON/XML macro-series retrieval and the real-time/vintage semantics required for point-in-time datasets and revision preservation.
sources.notes: Related pages: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html and https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_vintagedates.html . A free registered API key is required. HTTP 429 is documented, but a stable numeric quota was not found; use explicit vintages, conservative backoff, caching, and no identity rotation. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: BLS Public Data API versions, signatures, and usage-limit documentation family
sources.credibility_signals: BLS .gov primary developer documentation and service FAQ.
sources.freshness_signals: FAQ last modified 2023-08-30; service documentation accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Proves a free unregistered v1 baseline and documents optional registered v2 capabilities, request shapes, metadata differences, and exact quotas.
sources.notes: Related limits page: https://www.bls.gov/developers/api_faqs.htm . v1/v2 daily limits are 25/500; series limits 25/50; year limits 10/20; both allow 50 requests per 10 seconds. v2 registration includes a CAPTCHA and annual renewal, which must remain manual user steps. Batch and cache within limits; never bypass registration or rotate accounts. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data REST API and daily interest-rate XML/CSV documentation family
sources.source_type: official U.S. Treasury API and file documentation
sources.credibility_signals: Treasury .gov primary API registry, dataset documentation, feed guide, and developer change notice.
sources.freshness_signals: Current API registry and 2026 daily-rate pages accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Covers GET-only JSON datasets with field/filter/sort/pagination metadata and official XML/CSV yield, bill, long-term, and real-rate files.
sources.notes: Related pages: https://home.treasury.gov/treasury-daily-interest-rate-xml-feed and https://home.treasury.gov/developer-notice-xml-changes . The all-period XML feed uses zero-based pagination and a 300-row default. Fiscal Data values and null representations require explicit schema-driven parsing; HTTP 429 and historical URL/field changes require backoff, source health, and schema-change tests. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: tract-onnx pure-Rust inference documentation with ONNX Runtime support-status context
sources.source_type: maintainer-published project Rustdoc with upstream standard context
sources.credibility_signals: Current tract project Rustdoc; Microsoft's ONNX Runtime docs explicitly classify Rust APIs as external community projects.
sources.selection_rationale: Provides a no-cloud, no-Python, pure-Rust ONNX-compatible inference candidate while keeping first-party support and operator-coverage claims bounded.
sources.notes: Official Microsoft context: https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/get-started/community-projects.html . tract Rustdoc coverage was about 49%, and no universal operator/opset compatibility is promised. Validate model hash, opset, tensor schema, numerical equivalence, performance, and failure behavior per bundle; inference error must yield no action. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: FASB ASC 820 and IFRS 13 fair-value measurement authority family
sources.credibility_signals: Primary FASB amendment document plus IFRS Foundation issued-standard and implementation-support pages.
sources.freshness_signals: IFRS landing page marked Standard 2026 Issued; FASB current index and official PDF accessed 2026-07-15.
sources.selection_rationale: Defines Level 1 as accessible unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical items, establishes input hierarchy and lowest-significant-input treatment, and supports strict separation from execution quality.
sources.notes: Related official pages: https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-13-fair-value-measurement/ and https://www.ifrs.org/supporting-implementation/supporting-materials-by-ifrs-standards/ifrs-13/ . FASB states the Codification is authoritative and an ASU is not; complete current ASC/IFRS text may have license/sign-in restrictions. Store evidence, active/accessibility/identity/adjustment decisions, ruleset version, overrides, and approvals; do not redistribute standards or conflate hierarchy with market depth/data quality. Accessed 2026-07-15.
